mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: supply chain stress or recessionary environment
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflationary environment, which increases both discount rates and cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 3% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, boosting consumer demand and corporate earnings, and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month growth > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth exceeds 3% month-over-month for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 6-month moving averages signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall below their 6-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 forward returns at the 5-day horizon during non-recessionary regimes, as rising output signals improved corporate fundamentals and optimism.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO growth and S&P 500 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in non-recessionary periods.
